q: Should a chemical tanker operator count the empty return trip?
title: Chemical tankers: the empty return trip
short: Yes. Fuel burned driving back empty is part of the service, so it is counted and shared over the loads delivered. The GLEC Framework default intensities already include empty running; when you work from your own fuel records, add the return fuel yourself.
audience: Chemical and liquid road tanker operators and the shippers who hire them

ul: From fuel: add loaded and empty fuel for the round trip, then divide by tonnes delivered.
From defaults: tonne-km of the loaded leg times a GLEC intensity, which already includes empty running. Do not add the return again.

p: State which method you used. Mixing the two counts the empty leg twice.

example.title: Worked example: one round trip (illustrative inputs)
lines: Loaded leg: 105 L; empty return: 75 L
Delivered: 20 t, so 482.4 / 20 = 24.12 kg CO2 per tonne
example.note: Quantities are illustrative; use trip fuel records.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
